_purpose: ✒️ Executive Enactment Record — the action vocabulary and the source-of-record rule. Shipped as data (not buried in code) so the guards, the client renderer and the ingest Function all validate against ONE list, the way db/issue-keys.json already gates issue keys.
_whyClassesNeverMerge: Signing a bill Congress passed and issuing an order alone are different claims about power. A combined 'N actions' figure would flatten shared authorship into sole authorship, so counts are always reported per class and never summed into one headline number.

signed_law.label: Signed into law
signed_law.authorshipNote: Congress wrote and passed it; the signature endorsed it. Provisions are not individually endorsed — a multi-issue measure must show its per-issue directions.
signed_law.sourceOfRecord: congress.gov bill page, carrying the Public Law number and the presidential action date

vetoed_law.label: Vetoed
vetoed_law.authorshipNote: Blocked something Congress passed. The veto message is the statement of reasons and is part of the record.
vetoed_law.sourceOfRecord: congress.gov bill page plus the veto message

executive_order.label: Executive order
executive_order.authorshipNote: Acted alone under claimed executive authority. Sole authorship, and therefore the class where the Standing axis carries the greatest weight.
executive_order.sourceOfRecord: federalregister.gov document page — the permanent legal citation of record

directive.label: Directive
directive.authorshipNote: Presidential memorandum, proclamation or agency direction — acting alone with a lesser instrument than an executive order.

_measureTypesNote: Additive to the existing bill | resolution | amendment | nomination | litigation set on vr_measures.measure_type. Precedent: measureType='litigation' with chamber='court' already lets a non-roll-call actor share the issue spine.
_chambersNote: Additive to house | senate | joint | court.
_positionActionTypesNote: Additive to vr_positions.action_type (sponsor | cosponsor | amicus | plaintiff | committee_vote | statement). vr_positions is already documented as 'non-roll-call actions that still count as doing', which is exactly what an executive action is.

issueDirections.opposes: This action cuts against the issue.

_issueDirectionsNote: Reads vr_measure_issues.supportMeaning without renaming the column: yea_supports → advances, yea_opposes → opposes. Same data as the congressional lane, no vote word in the rendered vocabulary.

sourceRule._why: Fail closed. An action whose primary source is a directory index or a press summary cannot be verified by the reader, so it is not publishable — the same discipline every vr_* table applies with its NOT NULL source_url.
sourceRule._courtHostsWhy: Added in Phase 3, when the standing of the wave-1 orders had to be established from rulings rather than asserted. A federal court's own document server is as primary as a source gets, and storage.courtlistener.com serves the byte-identical PDF of the same opinion under a stable path — the Phase 3 pass verified that the April 2025 D.D.C. opinion downloads identically (816,214 bytes) from ecf.dcd.uscourts.gov and from storage.courtlistener.com. Reading a ruling is the only way to tell 'blocked' from 'partly blocked' from 'in force', so the host list has to reach the rulings.

_rejectedWhy.^https?://[^/]+/?$: A bare host root cites nothing. Found in live curated data on the judicial-appointments item (https://www.congress.gov/).
_rejectedWhy.^https?://[^/]+/presidential-actions/?$: A directory index, not a document. Found in live curated data on cut_spending and tariffs_growth.
_rejectedWhy./fact-sheet: A fact sheet is the administration describing its own order. Allowed as a labelled secondary link, never as the source of record. Found in live curated data on healthcare_costs.
